html:
The Apiaká are a Tupi-Guarani people of northern Mato Grosso in Brazil, near the border with Pará, on the Juruena and Teles Pires rivers.

Before the 1800s they were a warlike farming people, known for raids on their neighbours, including the Munduruku. Their numbers fell steeply from the mid 1800s with contact, disease and rubber collecting, and they were once thought extinct. Today several hundred live in their own reserve, near the Rikbaktsa, and most speak Portuguese. They are part of the wider family of Tupi peoples.
